tables.name: reservations
tables.description: One reservation table: a resource, a time range and a state (arch 09 line 457). EXCLUDE refuses overlapping held or booked time per worker, room or vehicle, and per worker person across businesses; class seats are counted in class_seats (arch 05 line 255; arch 10 line 510; BP section 10 card T-041). A saved time is a held row with held_until (arch 05 line 247); someone waiting next in line is a waiting row, and queued_at orders the line (A4-18).
tables.source: arch 09 line 457 ('Reservation: resource · range · state'); arch 05 lines 247, 255; arch 10 line 510; BP section 10 card T-041; FS line 743; key time_saved (A4-21, B4-23)

columns.description: When the row was written, never changed after; for a waiting row, its place in line. The next in line for a released time is the waiting row of that resource whose time overlaps it with the earliest queued_at, a tie broken by the lower id (ids stay opaque, CQ-09: compared only to break a tie, never parsed), so release promotes exactly one row and the same one every time.
columns.source: A4-18 and arch 05 line 247 ('A time someone else has saved: they wait next in line'); 02-contracts K-05 item 6 ('Release: ... promoting the next in line'; 'or next in line (A4-18)'); CQ-09 (ids are opaque, so no id gives the order)

columns.name: id

columns.description: The handle whose texts it batches (handles.id).

columns.name: event_ids
columns.description: The event ids of the texts it joins, in order (K-06).

columns.name: state
columns.description: leased, committed or parked.

columns.name: lease_until
columns.description: While leased, when the 60 s lease lapses; a lapsed lease reruns the turn from its sealed texts.

columns.name: bundle_hash
columns.description: The bundle the turn ran on (pinned at turn start). The hash half of K-01's bundleId: 64 lowercase hex characters.
columns.source: K-01 v1 bundleId (bundle.v1.schema.json manifest.bundleId); CQ-09; arch 10 line 548

columns.name: bundle_build
columns.description: The build half of K-01's bundleId, counting publishes from 1.

columns.name: trace_id
columns.description: The turn's trace id: the first text's (CQ-06).

columns.name: joined_trace_ids
columns.description: The other texts' trace ids, each ending at 'joined turn T' (CQ-06).

columns.name: tries
columns.description: How many times the turn has started; parked after a third crash before its commit.

columns.name: committed_at
columns.description: When it committed.

columns.name: parked_at
columns.description: When it was parked.

columns.name: version
columns.description: The row's version: every update raises it by one, and a commit compares and sets it, so a write made from an old read is refused with the rows that changed (limit 4).

checks.name: turns_leased_has_lease

checks.name: turns_tries_range

tables.name: outbox_rows
tables.description: One message to one recipient on one channel (arch 01 line 65): written at the commit with no plan, then the composer's plan and the final parts are written into it (arch 01 lines 39 to 41; arch 11 line 576). It stores K-03's plan and final parts as one JSON value each. K-07 gives the row's states and moves, and the parts' kinds; this table holds them as text. From v1.1 (ADR-016 section 1), work with no turn writes its row under its job id in place of a turn id (outbox_rows_turn_or_job): a sign-in's code row is written by one K-05 call, with its code-built plan and final parts, in one transaction. An email row may name its K-12 purpose, and a row may name the time from which no part of it is sent.
tables.source: arch 01 lines 39 to 41, 65; arch 02 lines 121 to 127; arch 07 lines 347, 371, 397; RULES 4.3; 02-contracts K-04 'Outbox rows'; K-03 v1 rowPlan, finalParts; ADR-016 section 1 (v1.1)

columns.name: id
columns.description: The outbox row's id: an opaque string code makes and never parses (CQ-09).

columns.name: turn_id
columns.description: The turn whose commit wrote it (turns.id); null for a row written by work with no turn, which names its job_id instead (v1.1; outbox_rows_turn_or_job). A made-up turn would break arch 01 line 59 (a turn is one batch of a handle's texts) and K-08's turn id (a hash of texts' event ids).
columns.source: arch 02 line 121; ADR-016 section 1 (arch 01 line 59; K-08 v1.1 default 9)

columns.name: commit_seq
columns.description: Commit order: the dispatcher sends each recipient's rows in this order. An identity column.
columns.source: arch 02 line 125; 02-contracts K-04 ('commit order per recipient')

columns.name: recipient_handle_id
columns.description: The recipient's handle (handles.id): a mobile, or an email address for an email row.

columns.name: recipient_person_id
columns.description: The recipient (persons.id), when known.

columns.name: business_id
columns.description: The business it is from or about (businesses.id); null for Rosie's own lines before there is one.

columns.name: booking_id
columns.description: The booking it is about (bookings.id), or null.

columns.name: channel
columns.description: imessage, rcs or sms through Linq, or email (K-03 v1's channel).
columns.source: arch 01 line 65; K-03 v1 channel; MC C9; DL-012

columns.name: send_class
columns.description: routine; quick_reply (a reply in the same turn: Q-15); visit_now (a visit happening now); safety. Only routine waits for text hours. From v1.1 a sign-in's code row, written with no turn, is quick_reply too: it answers the person's own request in the same call and dies 10 minutes after its code is made (ADR-016 section 3).
columns.source: RULES 4.3; arch 01 line 65; Q-15; ADR-016 section 3 (v1.1)

columns.name: versions_read
columns.description: The versions this was decided on: a JSON array of {"table", "rowId", "version"}, the row references of K-02's facts, which the commit compares and sets (limit 4).

columns.name: open_question_id
columns.description: The open question it asks (open_questions.id), or null.

columns.name: plan
columns.description: K-03 v1's rowPlan, as one JSON value; null until the composer's plan is written (only rows without a plan are composed after a crash).
columns.source: K-03 v1 rowPlan; arch 07 line 347; arch 11 line 576

columns.name: final_parts
columns.description: K-03 v1's finalParts, as one JSON value: the sends after code inserted options and fixed lines and filled slots; null until then.
columns.source: K-03 v1 finalParts; arch 02 line 123; arch 07 line 367

columns.name: copy_of_row_id
columns.description: For an email copy, the text row whose plan it reuses (outbox_rows.id).

columns.name: state
columns.description: Where the row stands; K-07 gives the values and moves.

columns.name: held_until
columns.description: Held for text hours until this time; later rows for the recipient may pass.

columns.name: bundle_hash
columns.description: The bundle of the turn that wrote it; for a row written by work with no turn (v1.1), the bundle active at that work's call, as K-08 v1.1 default 1 names it for a hop outside a turn. The hash half of K-01's bundleId: 64 lowercase hex characters.
columns.source: K-01 v1 bundleId (bundle.v1.schema.json manifest.bundleId); CQ-09; arch 10 line 548; K-08 v1.1 default 1 and ADR-016 section 1 (v1.1)

columns.name: bundle_build
columns.description: The build half of K-01's bundleId, counting publishes from 1.

columns.name: trace_id
columns.description: The trace id it rides under, from webhook to delivery receipt; for a row written by work with no turn (v1.1), that work's own trace, such as the page call's for a sign-in's code row.

columns.name: version
columns.description: The row's version: every update raises it by one, and a commit compares and sets it, so a write made from an old read is refused with the rows that changed (limit 4).

columns.name: job_id
columns.description: For a row written by work with no turn (v1.1): that work's id, in place of a turn id, as the event log's job_id and K-07's effect rows carry one. For a sign-in code's email row, the server-made id of its sign-in attempt (ADR-016 section 4, CQ-09), which the code's event-log entries carry too; never the page's attemptId, the code, its hash or the address. Later, a clock firing with no turn (CQ-28). Null on a row a turn's commit writes.
columns.source: ADR-016 sections 1 and 4 (K-08 v1.1 README: a page's rows carry its request or job id in job_id; K-05 README open gap 3); K-04 v1 event_log.job_id

columns.name: email_purpose
columns.description: For an email row, why it goes (v1.1): one of K-12 v1's six sendEmail purposes as K-12 spells them, confirmation, copy, emailWay, nextWay, code or notice. The email path reads it to know a code row (ADR-016 sections 3 and 5). Null on every row of a text channel (outbox_rows_email_purpose_is_email), and on an email row whose writer names no purpose, as no v1 writer does.
columns.source: ADR-016 sections 1, 3 and 5; K-12 v1 README (sendEmail.request purpose)

columns.name: not_after
columns.description: No part of the row is sent at or after this time (v1.1): limit 8 withdraws the row at any try at or after it, a first try, a retry or a late wake, and sends nothing. A row of purpose code holds one, its code's expires_at, 10 minutes after the code is made (outbox_rows_code_has_not_after); null: no such time.
columns.source: ADR-016 sections 1 and 3; RULES 6.2; K-22 v1 proof_codes.expires_at (proof_codes_ten_minutes)

checks.name: outbox_rows_turn_or_job
checks.expression: turn_id is not null or job_id is not null
checks.source: ADR-016 section 1; the event log's own rule (K-04 v1 event_log_turn_or_job; 0011 line 53)

checks.name: outbox_rows_email_purpose_known
checks.expression: email_purpose is null or email_purpose in ('confirmation', 'copy', 'emailWay', 'nextWay', 'code', 'notice')
checks.source: ADR-016 section 1 (one of K-12 v1's six purposes); K-12 v1 README (sendEmail.request purpose)

checks.name: outbox_rows_email_purpose_is_email
checks.source: ADR-016 section 1 (a purpose on an email row only)

checks.name: outbox_rows_code_has_not_after
checks.expression: email_purpose is null or email_purpose <> 'code' or not_after is not null
checks.source: ADR-016 sections 1 and 3 (a code dies 10 minutes after it is made, and a retry never sends a dead code); RULES 6.2

indexes.name: outbox_rows_recipient_order_idx

tables.description: One part of an outbox row under one idempotency key (row, part, try): Linq's message and option ids and what happened to it (arch 01 line 65). A retry after a timeout or crash reuses the key (attempts rises); one after a reported failure gets a new key, the next try. K-07 gives the kinds, states and retry rules. From v1.1 a delivered part holds its delivery time (outbox_parts_delivered_has_time; CQ-211).
tables.source: arch 01 line 65; arch 07 line 367; 02-contracts K-04 'Outbox rows'; 02-contracts K-07; CQ-211 (v1.1)

columns.name: failed_at

columns.name: error_code
columns.description: The provider's error code, such as 4001 or 4006.

columns.name: version
columns.description: The row's version: every update raises it by one, and a commit compares and sets it, so a write made from an old read is refused with the rows that changed (limit 4).

checks.name: outbox_parts_delivered_has_time
checks.expression: state <> 'delivered' or delivered_at is not null
checks.source: CQ-211's default (K-04's next minor version adds it); ADR-016 section 1; arch 02 line 127

indexes.name: outbox_parts_linq_message_idx
indexes.why: Delivery receipts find their part by Linq's message id (arch 02 line 127).

K-08 gives its kinds and the shape of why, approved by and proofs.

At turn start the actor reads the active bundle id from PostgreSQL, then that bundle's values from KV, or from bundle_values on a miss (arch 10 line 536). The deploy publishes a bundle before it switches the active id (BP 5.4). Every published bundle stays readable for replay (tour line 658).
tables.source: CQ-03 (the bundle registry); arch 10 line 536; arch 01 line 87; BP 5.4; tour line 658; K-01 v1 manifest.bundleId and storage

tables.name: sealing_keys
tables.description: Per-person sealing keys: private values are encrypted under the person's key, so deleting the key erases them (arch 01 line 93; arch 09 line 492; RULES 4.10). The key is stored wrapped under a key kept in Workers secrets, which this table names and never holds (rule 7). Erasing keeps the row with the wrapped key gone.
tables.source: arch 01 line 93; arch 09 line 492; arch 10 line 516; RULES 4.10; CQ-03

columns.name: person_id
columns.description: The person (persons.id).

columns.name: wrapped_key
columns.description: The person's data key, encrypted under the wrapping key; null once erased.

columns.name: wrapping_key_name
columns.description: The name of the Workers secret that wraps it: a name, never a value.
columns.source: arch 10 line 546 (secrets in Workers secrets); BP rule 7

columns.name: created_at
columns.description: When the key was made.

columns.name: erased_at
columns.description: When the key was deleted, erasing the person's sealed values.

columns.name: version
columns.description: The row's version: every update raises it by one, and a commit compares and sets it, so a write made from an old read is refused with the rows that changed (limit 4).

rowLevelSecurity.why: A person's key covers them at every business (FS line 743).
